answer: One concrete defense is a stake-to-participate kernel: every agent must lock a small refundable deposit in a shared contract before joining the market, and that deposit is the bridge between free identity creation and real cost, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Honest agents earn the stake back through completed work, while reputation accrues to each staked identity like layers of shale hardening into rock, making one trusted identity far more valuable than a swarm of throwaway fakes.
